stages.name: Define Strategy
stages.intro: Convert readiness evidence into an enterprise ambition, operating model and sequenced roadmap.
stages.executiveQuestion: What will AI change for the enterprise, how much ambition is justified, and which outcomes will leadership own?
inputs: AI principles, risk appetite and funding parameters
risks: Aspirational targets unsupported by readiness evidence
Unclear build, buy and partner boundaries
measures: Percentage of outcomes with baselines and owners
questions: What will AI change for the enterprise, how much ambition is justified, and which outcomes will leadership own?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Enterprise AI Strategy Decision Pack?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
stages.why: Readiness identifies what the enterprise can support; strategy decides what it will pursue and deliberately decline.
stages.separation: Unlike Assess Readiness, this stage makes forward-looking choices about ambition, operating model and investment horizons.
stages.prevents: Prevents disconnected pilots, technology-first commitments and targets that cannot be supported by evidence.
activities: Translate readiness gaps into explicit strategic choices
Set outcome owners, baseline needs and strategic measures
Choose build, buy and partner boundaries
Sequence capability, governance and investment horizons
governance: Record strategic assumptions with review dates
Require one accountable executive for each outcome
Escalate choices outside approved risk appetite
dependencies: Readiness conditions constrain the roadmap
Governance converts principles into enforceable controls
Opportunity selection applies the approved outcomes
entry: Readiness disposition is approved
Material evidence gaps have resolution owners
Enterprise priorities and constraints are current
exit: Strategic choices and rejected alternatives are recorded
Outcome ownership and measurement approach are approved
Roadmap horizons are authorised for portfolio planning
stages.guidance: Use AI to compare documented strategic options and expose contradictory assumptions. Do not use generated market forecasts as enterprise evidence.
configuration: Accountable executive — organisation to confirm
Target outcomes — define with business owners
Strategic review cadence — configure through enterprise planning

stages.name: Establish Governance
stages.intro: Turn principles and risk appetite into usable decision rights, policies, controls and assurance.
stages.executiveQuestion: Can every material AI decision be made by the right authority using sufficient evidence and enforceable controls?
risks: Controls applied uniformly regardless of impact
questions: Can every material AI decision be made by the right authority using sufficient evidence and enforceable controls?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Governance and Control Framework?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
roles: Legal, Privacy and Security — own controls
Business and Technology Owners — accept decisions
stages.why: A strategy cannot be delivered responsibly until decision rights and control evidence are embedded in normal work.
stages.separation: Unlike Define Strategy, this stage turns direction and risk appetite into operating rules, authorities and assurance paths.
stages.prevents: Prevents unowned AI decisions, inconsistent controls and exceptions that remain invisible until release.
activities: Map AI decisions to accountable authorities
Define proportionate controls by impact classification
Establish intake, inventory and exception workflows
Map obligations to evidence and assurance owners
governance: Maintain one authoritative AI inventory
Require independent challenge for high-impact uses
Time-limit exceptions and document compensating controls
dependencies: Strategy defines boundaries and desired outcomes
Architecture must implement control requirements
Operations supplies continuous assurance evidence
entry: Strategy and risk appetite are approved
Existing policy and assurance forums are mapped
Potentially applicable obligations are identified
exit: Decision rights and escalation paths are approved
Control owners and evidence requirements are assigned
Classification, intake and exception workflows are usable
stages.guidance: AI may assist with mapping documented obligations to controls. Qualified owners must confirm applicability and legal meaning.
configuration: Accountable governance authority — organisation to confirm
Applicable regulation — select by jurisdiction and industry
Approval thresholds — configure to delegated authority

stages.name: Identify and Prioritise Opportunities
stages.intro: Build a governed portfolio balancing strategic value, feasibility, adoption effort, risk and learning.
stages.executiveQuestion: Which opportunities deserve scarce investment now, which should be explored, and which should be stopped?
risks: Adoption cost or affected people ignored
questions: Which opportunities deserve scarce investment now, which should be explored, and which should be stopped?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Prioritised Opportunity Portfolio?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
stages.why: Enterprise value depends on choosing a coherent portfolio, not approving every plausible use case independently.
stages.separation: Unlike Establish Governance, this stage applies controls and strategy to compare business opportunities and allocate attention.
stages.prevents: Prevents duplicated use cases, sponsor-driven prioritisation and portfolios that ignore adoption or shared dependencies.
activities: Frame business problems without prescribing a model or vendor
Assess value, feasibility, data, risk and workforce impact
Consolidate overlapping opportunities around shared capability
Record select, explore, defer and stop decisions
governance: Use the same published criteria across candidates
Separate evidence confidence from scoring preference
Re-score when scope, dependency or risk changes
dependencies: Strategy supplies outcomes and portfolio principles
Governance supplies classification and review thresholds
Business cases validate shortlisted investments
entry: Opportunity owners and affected groups are identified
Prioritisation criteria are approved
Evidence confidence can be recorded
exit: Portfolio choices and rationale are approved
Shortlisted opportunities have accountable sponsors
Deferred and rejected opportunities remain traceable
stages.guidance: Use AI to cluster similar opportunity statements and test scoring consistency; business owners retain responsibility for value and impact.
configuration: Portfolio authority — organisation to confirm
Scoring weights — configure to strategic priorities
Capacity envelope — confirm through portfolio planning

stages.name: Build the Business Case
stages.intro: Make value, lifecycle cost, risk, uncertainty and delivery commitment transparent.
stages.executiveQuestion: Is the expected value worth the total enterprise commitment and residual risk?
risks: Run, assurance and change costs omitted
questions: Is the expected value worth the total enterprise commitment and residual risk?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Enterprise AI Business Case?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
stages.why: A prioritised opportunity is not yet an investable commitment; leadership needs transparent economics and uncertainty.
stages.separation: Unlike opportunity prioritisation, this stage validates the full lifecycle commitment for a specific investment decision.
stages.prevents: Prevents unfunded operating obligations, double-counted benefits and optimistic cases built from vendor claims.
activities: Confirm benefit baselines, owners and attribution
Estimate build, run, data, assurance and change costs
Compare viable options and the do-nothing consequence
Define funding tranches and evidence-based continuation triggers
governance: Use ranges and confidence rather than false precision
Validate benefits independently from suppliers
Tie subsequent funding to evidence and decision triggers
dependencies: Prioritised briefs define the business problem
Architecture options refine feasibility and cost
Operations later reports realised benefits and unit cost
entry: Opportunity priority and sponsor are confirmed
A credible baseline and viable options exist
Material constraints and control obligations are known
exit: Benefits, costs and sensitivities are reviewable
Funding, benefit and residual-risk owners are named
Investment decision and release conditions are recorded
stages.guidance: AI can identify missing cost categories and compare documented scenarios. Finance must validate source figures, attribution and sensitivity assumptions.
configuration: Approval threshold — configure to delegated authority
Target benefit — define during business-case approval
Funding release conditions — organisation to confirm

stages.name: Design the Target Architecture
stages.intro: Translate strategy, investment and controls into an implementable, secure and operable target state.
stages.executiveQuestion: Will the design deliver the outcome, integrate with the enterprise and remain operable over its full life?
workspaces: Application, integration and AI platform design
questions: Will the design deliver the outcome, integrate with the enterprise and remain operable over its full life?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Target Architecture Decision Pack?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
roles: Security, Data and Privacy — own domains
stages.why: Approved value and controls must be translated into a coherent design before delivery teams make irreversible choices.
stages.separation: Unlike the Business Case, this stage decides how capabilities, data, systems, models, controls and people fit together.
stages.prevents: Prevents prototypes becoming production architecture, hidden vendor lock-in and controls that cannot be tested.
activities: Define target capabilities, boundaries and transition states
Select data, model, integration and human-oversight patterns
Threat-model the complete service and operating context
Record decisions, alternatives, exceptions and exit provisions
governance: Trace each mandatory control to a design component
Record vendor concentration and portability decisions
Route deviations through architecture authority
dependencies: Business case fixes the approved scope and value case
Governance defines mandatory controls
Implementation planning consumes approved decisions
entry: Investment scope and design authority are approved
Current-state dependencies are owned
Architecture principles and controls are available
exit: Target and transition architectures are approved
Material decisions and exceptions are recorded
The design is estimable, testable and operable
stages.guidance: AI may compare approved patterns and check design completeness. Architects remain accountable for integration effects and threat assumptions.
configuration: Architecture authority — organisation to confirm
Approved technology standards — select from enterprise catalogue
Resilience targets — define by service criticality

stages.name: Plan Implementation
stages.intro: Create one realistic plan spanning technology, data, controls, testing, workforce change and transition.
stages.executiveQuestion: Is the organisation ready to commit people, funding and accountable ownership to a controlled delivery plan?
questions: Is the organisation ready to commit people, funding and accountable ownership to a controlled delivery plan?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Integrated Implementation Plan?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
stages.why: An approved design still fails when technology, data, controls, change and transition are planned separately.
stages.separation: Unlike Target Architecture, this stage converts design decisions into an integrated, resourced and controlled delivery baseline.
stages.prevents: Prevents late assurance, uncommitted dependencies and technical delivery without adoption or service readiness.
activities: Decompose the design into owned increments and milestones
Integrate data, control, test, change and transition work
Commit environments, procurement and specialist capacity
Define evidence gates, contingencies and change control
governance: Baseline scope, cost, schedule and benefits together
Include assurance work in the critical path
Escalate material variance through change authority
dependencies: Architecture provides approved components and constraints
Business case provides funding conditions
Build teams require committed access, data and environments
entry: Architecture and funding decisions are approved
Delivery and service owners accept accountability
Critical dependencies can be scheduled
exit: Integrated baseline is approved and resourced
Test, adoption and transition work is funded
Contingencies and decision points are explicit
stages.guidance: AI can challenge plan completeness and summarise dependencies, but it must not invent estimates, commitments or resource availability.
configuration: Programme authority — organisation to confirm
Schedule tolerance — configure through programme controls
Resource commitments — confirm with accountable functions

stages.name: Build and Integrate
stages.intro: Build and integrate the solution while preserving traceability from requirements and controls to evidence.
stages.executiveQuestion: Is delivery producing the approved solution with controlled change, secure engineering and evidence fit for validation?
questions: Is delivery producing the approved solution with controlled change, secure engineering and evidence fit for validation?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Build and Configuration Evidence?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
stages.why: Controlled engineering is needed to preserve the approved design and create evidence that validation can trust.
stages.separation: Unlike Plan Implementation, this stage produces and integrates the actual release candidate under configuration control.
stages.prevents: Prevents undocumented prompt changes, sensitive data leakage and technical debt hidden until production.
activities: Build components in reviewable, traceable increments
Implement security, oversight and observability with the service
Version models, prompts, data and configuration
Maintain runbooks, limitations, defects and provenance
governance: Protect source, artefacts, secrets and development data
Approve material design changes before implementation
Maintain provenance for models and third-party components
dependencies: Implementation plan supplies acceptance criteria
Architecture decisions constrain component choices
Testing consumes stable, versioned artefacts
entry: Design, environments and access are approved
Engineering and data-handling standards operate
Requirements and controls are traceable
exit: Integrated release candidate is versioned
Known defects and deviations are assessed
Build evidence and operational documentation are complete
stages.guidance: Use only approved AI engineering tools. Review generated code, protect enterprise data and record material model or library dependencies.
configuration: Engineering owner — organisation to confirm
Approved development tools — select through security review
Defect tolerance — define in the test strategy

stages.name: Test and Validate
stages.intro: Prove the service is functional, safe, secure, usable, resilient and supportable under realistic conditions.
stages.executiveQuestion: Does independent evidence justify exposing people, operations and enterprise data to this release?
workspaces: AI quality, safety and human factors
questions: Does independent evidence justify exposing people, operations and enterprise data to this release?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Production Readiness Evidence Pack?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
roles: Risk and Service Owners — accept exposure
stages.why: A working build is not evidence that an AI-enabled service is safe, fair, resilient or fit for real operating conditions.
stages.separation: Unlike Build and Integrate, this stage independently challenges claims and determines whether a release candidate is acceptable.
stages.prevents: Prevents average metrics hiding critical failures, unrealistic test data and untested human escalation.
activities: Execute risk-based functional and integration tests
Evaluate AI quality across representative and adverse scenarios
Test security, privacy, recovery and human intervention
Reconcile defects, limitations and residual risk
governance: Preserve testing independence proportionate to impact
Document representativeness and known limitations
Require authorised exceptions for unresolved critical defects
dependencies: Build supplies a stable release candidate
Governance supplies control acceptance requirements
Deployment planning must address accepted limitations
entry: Release candidate and test environments are controlled
Acceptance criteria and test data are approved
Independent reviewers are available where required
exit: Required tests pass or exceptions are authorised
Residual risks and limitations are communicated
Evidence supports an accountable release decision
stages.guidance: AI can propose test cases and help analyse results. Test owners must validate coverage, expected outcomes and conclusions.
configuration: Release acceptance authority — organisation to confirm
Performance thresholds — define by use-case risk
Representative groups and scenarios — confirm with affected owners

stages.name: Deploy and Transition
stages.intro: Release safely and transfer accountable ownership, knowledge and control evidence into operations.
stages.executiveQuestion: Can the organisation release without losing control, continuity or clear accountability?
questions: Can the organisation release without losing control, continuity or clear accountability?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Transition and Ownership Record?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
stages.why: Release changes real work, accountability and exposure; a technically accepted system still requires controlled cutover and ownership.
stages.separation: Unlike Test and Validate, this stage moves the accepted release into production and transfers responsibility from delivery to service operation.
stages.prevents: Prevents orphaned services, unusable rollback plans and users operating without limits or escalation routes.
activities: Complete go-live readiness and authority checks
Execute cutover, verification and rollback controls
Transfer access, records, runbooks and ownership
Operate heightened monitoring and early-life support
governance: Do not release without named service and risk owners
Record the actual production configuration and approvals
Retain rollback authority during early-life support
dependencies: Validation provides accepted evidence and limitations
Operations requires access, monitoring and runbooks
Change teams prepare users and affected processes
entry: Release candidate and residual risk are accepted
Cutover and rollback are rehearsed
Business, service and control owners accept their roles
exit: Production state and release decision are recorded
Support, monitoring and ownership are active
Early-life issues and adoption signals are controlled
stages.guidance: AI may assist with approved communications and runbook checks; it must not make autonomous release or rollback decisions.
configuration: Release authority — organisation to confirm
Early-life support period — define by service risk
Rollback trigger — configure in the release plan

stages.name: Operate and Govern Production
stages.intro: Run the service with monitoring, accountable decisions, incident response, control evidence and value tracking.
stages.executiveQuestion: Does continued operation remain safe, compliant, reliable and valuable as conditions change?
measures: Benefits, unit cost and control effectiveness
questions: Does continued operation remain safe, compliant, reliable and valuable as conditions change?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Production Assurance Report?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
roles: Model and Data Owners — manage quality
stages.why: AI performance, data, usage and threats change after release, so approval must be sustained through evidence and response.
stages.separation: Unlike Deploy and Transition, this stage owns continuing service health, control effectiveness, cost and business outcomes.
stages.prevents: Prevents silent drift, unattended control failures and fragmented accountability across enterprise and suppliers.
activities: Monitor technical, AI, business and control indicators
Investigate drift, harmful outcomes, complaints and incidents
Govern model, prompt, data and configuration changes
Review residual risk, cost, benefit and continued operation
governance: Treat material model, data or use changes as governed changes
Tie monitoring signals to owners and response thresholds
Reassess classification when scope or impact changes
dependencies: Transition establishes ownership and baselines
Benefits plan defines value measures
Improvement decisions require trustworthy operating evidence
entry: Ownership, monitoring and support are active
Response playbooks and thresholds are approved
Benefit and control reporting has a cadence
exit: Current assurance supports continued operation
Material issues have controlled responses
Evidence supports improve, scale, restrict or retire decisions
stages.guidance: AI can summarise telemetry and assist triage. Accountable owners must validate alerts, causes and material operating decisions.
configuration: Service-level targets — organisation to confirm
Monitoring thresholds — define from validation evidence
Assurance cadence — configure by impact classification

stages.name: Improve and Scale
stages.intro: Use production evidence to improve, reuse capability, scale responsibly and retire services that no longer justify operation.
stages.executiveQuestion: Where should the enterprise improve, scale, standardise, contain or retire based on realised evidence?
inputs: Incident, feedback, cost and performance trends
measures: Reuse and marginal cost of scale
Risk and control trend after change
questions: Where should the enterprise improve, scale, standardise, contain or retire based on realised evidence?
What evidence is sufficient to approve Benefits and Scale Decision Pack?
Which trade-offs and residual risks must be made explicit?
What conditions would require this stage to pause or return to earlier work?
roles: Business and Service Owners — own outcomes
stages.why: Operating evidence creates value only when it changes investment, design, reuse or retirement decisions.
stages.separation: Unlike Operate and Govern Production, this stage decides how learning changes the service and the wider enterprise portfolio.
stages.prevents: Prevents premature scaling, activity-based success claims and abandoned models, data or access remaining after retirement.
activities: Compare realised outcomes with approved baselines
Prioritise improvements using incidents, feedback and cost
Assess repeatability, shared capability and marginal cost
Approve scale, redesign, containment, renewal or retirement
governance: Re-enter earlier lifecycle gates for material changes
Do not inherit approval when scope, impact or data changes
Plan safe model, data, access and vendor retirement
dependencies: Operations supplies verified performance and benefit evidence
Portfolio planning consumes reusable learning
Material redesign loops through governance and architecture
entry: Sufficient operating evidence is available
Benefits and costs can be compared with baselines
Material incidents and limitations are understood
exit: Improvement or scale decision and rationale are approved
Work has accountable owners and control conditions
Retirement obligations are planned where applicable
stages.guidance: AI can surface patterns across approved evidence. Leadership must challenge attribution, survivor bias and whether local results are repeatable.
configuration: Scale authority — organisation to confirm
Target benefit — validate against realised baseline
Retirement retention obligations — confirm with records, legal and privacy owners
